gaps.criterion: Six purposes registered idempotently at boot
gaps.gap: All six are defined, the provisioner runs on every boot beside the role provisioner, and idempotency is proven by a test that answers 409 to every call and asserts six already_present with zero created. Not yet true against a live tenant: no ProjexCloud gateway is reachable here, so provisionConsentPurposes returns six skipped results and sdk-consent holds nothing. One boot with the gateway configured closes it. Worth carrying with it: until the purposes exist upstream the capture path should REFUSE to record consent rather than record it against an unregistered purpose - a receipt naming a purpose nobody registered looks like evidence and cannot be honoured on revocation. That refusal belongs in the capture path and is not built.

gaps.criterion: Every audit entry carries actor, purpose, decision, evidence and causation
gaps.gap: The HELPER enforces it and cannot be called otherwise: all seven fields - actor, personaRole, purpose, decisionRef, evidenceRef, causationId and idempotencyRef - are required on AuditEntry, so an entry missing any of them does not compile, and a test asserts the outbound wire shape so it cannot drift. What is not true is the word EVERY: no governed action calls appendAuditEntry yet. Capture, routing, assignment, first-response, import and identity actions all still complete without writing an entry, so the vocabulary and the helper exist ahead of their callers. This is the same shape as the PDP gap - the mechanism is built and unwired - and the two should be applied to the mutating handlers in one pass, since both want the same insertion point and the audit entry wants the PDP's decisionRef.

gaps.criterion: Nightly chain verification runs and opens an incident on mismatch
gaps.gap: The VERIFICATION is built and tested in all three states: an intact chain, a mismatch that opens an sdk-incident carrying the detail, and - the one most likely to mislead - an unreachable verifier reported as NOT intact, so a silent outage cannot masquerade as a clean bill of health. What is missing is NIGHTLY. Nothing schedules verifyAuditChain: there is no cron entry, no scheduler and no worker, so it runs only if something calls it, which nothing does. Closing this needs a scheduled trigger and a record of the last run, so that a verification which stops happening is itself visible - a silent scheduler is the same failure as a silent outage.
